comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 **Update 2026-10-22: every SFT arm trained on the GLM 5.3 traces scores below its parent on the agentic screens. Two next steps: re-run the cheap arms on the contributor (Kimi/Qwen) traces, and check the learning rate on the real rows.**

## Results on the GLM 5.3 traces

Screens are SWE-bench Verified random-100 and the TBLite 100-task subset (solved out of 100; TBLite timeouts count as failures), GSM8K and BFCL-Parity for retention. "Composite" is our screening mean (SWE + TBLite)/2, shown as a range when trials were unscored for infrastructure reasons; it is a bound, not a confidence interval. HIGH and LOW are the GLM reasoning-effort settings used to generate the traces; rows are token-matched per arm.

| model | parent | rows | SWE-bench r100 (submits) | TBLite-100 | GSM8K | BFCL | composite |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| parent v0.1 | – | – | 26 (36) | 23 | 91.1 | 32/123 | 24.5-25.0 |
| plain | v0.1 | HIGH | 13 (4) | 8 | 92.3 | 67/123 | 10.5-11.5 |
| plain | v0.1 | LOW | 17 (27) | 12 | 91.7 | 55/121 | 14.5-18.0 |
| relay | v0.1 | LOW | 25 (25) | 15 | 92.9 | 64/123 | 20.0-21.0 |
| parent v0 | – | – | 33 (56) | 20 | 85.2 | 27/122 | 26.5-27.0 |
| plain | v0 | HIGH | 17 (3) | 9 | 87.7 | 44/122 | 13.0-17.5 |
| plain, cut to the relay arm's token count | v0 | HIGH | 13 (6) | 11 | 91.1 | 54/123 | 12.0-12.5 |
| RS-multi | v0 | HIGH | 11 (6) | 10 | 89.9 | 41/123 | 10.5-11.0 |
| recovery | v0 | HIGH | 12 (4) | 9 | 88.5 | 48/123 | 10.5-11.0 |
| relay | v0 | HIGH | 13 (1) | 14 | 89.0 | 48/123 | 13.5-14.0 |
| plateau dropping | v0 | HIGH | 14 (6) | 13 | 89.8 | 49/123 | 13.5 |

What the data say:
- Every arm is below its parent on SWE-bench and TBLite and above it on GSM8K and BFCL. The regression is specific to the agentic tasks.
- Paired per-task differences on the frozen task lists (task bootstrap, 95%): no HIGH-row method differs from plain on either screen (SWE-bench -3 to -6 [about -13, +4]; TBLite 0 to +3 [about -6, +9]). Relay on the LOW rows beats plain on the LOW rows on SWE-bench by +8 [+1, +16], the only method-versus-twin interval that excludes zero; on TBLite +1 [-6, +7]. Every student is below its parent on SWE-bench (HIGH-row arms -13 to -22, intervals exclude zero; LOW relay -1 [-10, +8]) and most are below on TBLite.
- Relay on the LOW rows is therefore the strongest arm (25 SWE-bench vs the parent's 26), with the caveat that its recipe differs from plain's (963 vs 675 updates at equal tokens, student prefix masked) and that LOW rows hold 11.6M supervised tokens per epoch against HIGH's 19.4M.
- Mechanism, measured on trajectories: students keep the rows' per-step style (about 120 tokens per step, same command mix) but take about twice the rows' steps, run into the 32k window (75-97% of episodes) and rarely submit (HIGH-trained 3-6%, LOW-trained about 25%, parents 36-56%). Submitting is where the score comes from.
- The two parents are not distinguishable on the frozen task lists: paired SWE-bench difference v0 minus v0.1 = +7 [-2, +16], TBLite -3 [-12, +6] (task bootstrap). Of the 49 TBLite tasks where v0.1 timed out, v0 solved 3, so v0.1's timeouts are mostly hard tasks, not lost score (#10338: tripling the limit changed its score by one task).

Limits: one run per arm, 100 tasks per screen (about 4 points of standard error), TBLite timeout-bound for every student.

## Next step 1: the same cheap arms on the contributor traces

The one run of this recipe that beat its parent was the learning-rate sweep's 1e-6 run on the pilot traces (Qwen3.6-27B TMax episodes and Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith episodes, the data the contributors' original experiments used): composite 31.0-32.0 against v0's 26.5-27.0, TBLite 29 vs 20. That run used the sweep's sampler and exposure, not the arm recipe, so it is suggestive, not a control. The pilot rows also look different from the GLM rows: 14 steps per episode at 246 tokens per step with 28% reasoning tokens (HIGH: 25 steps, 120 tokens, 39%), and they are in Terminus-2 format, which never contains the mini-swe-agent submit command, yet that student kept 40% submits.

Plan: convert the pilot traces to the arm row format and train plain, RS-multi and recovery from v0.1 at 1e-6 under the arm recipe, plus plain from v0 as the bridge to the sweep. v0.1 is the base because it carries no relay graft and v0 was trained on about half of the pilot SWE tasks through the relay data grafted into it. Known limits: the Kimi SWE set has one trajectory per task, so RS-multi runs on TMax only; recovery needs an error style for Qwen's native tool calls; about 1,500 pilot SWE tasks have only the pilot's own decontamination check. Target: plain results within a day of the rows, the other two a day later.

## Next step 2: learning rate on the real rows

The sweep tied 3e-7, 1e-6 and 3e-6 on the pilot rows and 1e-6 was frozen without the planned confirmation on real plain rows. Two checks are running: plain SFT on the LOW v0 rows at 3e-7, paired against the 1e-6 twin (same rows, parent and schedule), to test whether gentler updates preserve more of the parent; and a screen of the HIGH plain v0.1 epoch-2 checkpoint against its final, as an update-dose check. A higher rate is not excluded but is the less likely direction given the sweep.

Also in flight: plain, relay and plateau on the LOW rows from v0, and RS-multi and recovery on the LOW rows from v0.1, to complete the LOW comparison on both parents. Models so far are on the Hub under `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-SFT-Shootout-*` (private). Design: [SFT comparison doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/13duCN6reb7KVLhBi8TszTL1EYKeaV3SEMQhl9IJCZSM/edit).

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 **Update 2026-10-24: on the same tasks, the contributor traces beat our GLM 5.3 traces by 26 SWE-bench tasks. The task pool does not explain the gap. Plateau dropping on contributor rows changes nothing.**

Terms:
- **LOW rows:** our GLM 5.3 traces at low reasoning effort.
- **Contributor rows:** the Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith and Qwen3.6-27B TMax traces from the learning-rate sweep.
- **lowshared / contribshared:** plain SFT on only the 1,432 tasks both row sets cover (466 SWE + 966 TMax). Matched on tasks, not tokens: the contributor side has 5.73M supervised tokens against 4.51M (1.27×).
- **Composite:** our screening mean, (SWE-bench r100 + TBLite-100)/2; a range when trials were unscored.

All arms from v0.1, LR 1e-6, 3 epochs.

| model | rows | GSM8K | SWE-bench r100 (submits) | TBLite-100 | BFCL | composite |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| parent v0.1 | – | 91.1 | 26 (36) | 23 | 32/123 | 24.5-25.0 |
| contributor plain | contributor, all | 94.0 | 29 (32) | 28/99 | 71/123 | 28.5-29.0 |
| LOW plain | LOW, all | 91.7 | 17 (27) | 12/93 | 55/121 | 14.5-18.0 |
| contribshared | contributor, shared tasks | 92.9 | 36 (46) | 18 | 80/123 | 27.0 |
| lowshared | LOW, shared tasks | 92.8 | 10 (12) | 9/98 | 62/123 | 9.5-10.5 |
| plateau dropping | contributor, all | 93.9 | 29 (41) | 30 | 74/123 | 29.5 |

Paired per-task differences (task bootstrap, 95%):

| comparison | SWE-bench | TBLite |
|---|---|---|
| contribshared − lowshared (the matched pair) | **+26 [+17, +36]** | **+9 [+1, +17]** |
| contribshared − parent v0.1 | **+10 [+1, +19]** | −5 [−15, +4] |
| lowshared − parent v0.1 | **−16 [−24, −8]** | **−14 [−22, −6]** |
| lowshared − LOW plain | −7 [−14, +0] | −4 [−11, +2] |
| plateau dropping − contributor plain | +0 [−7, +7] | +2 [−7, +11] |

What the data say:
- On identical tasks, GLM LOW rows push the student far below the parent, and contributor rows lift it above the parent on SWE-bench. The contributor-side +10 is the first gap against the parent that clears noise.
- Less GLM data does not help. lowshared used 39% of LOW plain's tokens and is not closer to the parent; 85 of its 100 SWE-bench episodes hit the context limit and it submitted 12 times. A lower learning rate (3e-7: SWE −7 [−13, −1] against 1e-6) and an earlier checkpoint (2 of 3 epochs: +5 [−4, +13]) also did not rescue the GLM rows.
- On contributor rows, plain, RS-multi, recovery and plateau dropping are indistinguishable.
- Limits: single runs on 100 tasks; the pair is matched on tasks, not tokens; read the small-budget pair for the gap, not for absolute levels.

Not tested: what remains between the row sets is the teacher (GLM 5.3 against Kimi/Qwen) and the harness format. Our GLM rows use each eval's own action protocol; the contributor rows use the other one.

Trace decontamination: the trained trace text was checked against the 100 SWE-bench gold and test patches and the 100 TBLite tests and solutions. There were 3 flags, all TBLite, all generic code (imports, a file-reading loop). Nothing was excluded.

Cost of these runs: 184.9 H100-h training and 106.4 H100-h screens. Documented total for the experiment: about 6,070 H100-h (a partial subtotal, not an invoice).

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 **Summary: no SFT method beat plain SFT by enough to matter; the source of the traces decided the result. The experiment is stopped and written up.**

## What we did

We compared plain SFT, rejection-sampled SFT (RS-multi), relay, recovery and plateau dropping for agentic coding on Snowball v0 and v0.1. The task pool was about 2,200 TMax and 2,100 SWE-smith tasks. Traces came from GLM 5.3 at three reasoning efforts, then from the contributor traces (Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith, Qwen3.6-27B TMax). Screens: SWE-bench Verified random-100, TBLite-100, GSM8K and BFCL-Parity.

## What we found

1. **Every arm trained on GLM 5.3 traces scored below its parent** on SWE-bench and TBLite, while gaining on GSM8K and BFCL. The students took about twice the steps of their training traces, ran into the 32k context limit in most SWE-bench episodes and rarely submitted.
2. **Methods mattered little.** Only relay on LOW rows beat plain SFT (SWE-bench +8 [+1, +16]), and it still trailed its parent. On contributor rows, plain, RS-multi, recovery and plateau dropping were indistinguishable.
3. **The rows mattered most.** With the same 1,432 tasks, parent and recipe, contributor rows beat GLM LOW rows by SWE-bench +26 [+17, +36] and TBLite +9 [+1, +17]. The contributor side also beat parent v0.1 on SWE-bench by +10 [+1, +19].
4. **Less GLM exposure did not help.** A lower learning rate, an earlier checkpoint and a smaller subset all stayed below the parent.

## Hypotheses (untested)

Why the GLM arms lost while the contributor rows gained, and why collaborators got large SFT gains from Kimi and Qwen traces on a weaker Snowball parent ([blog post, 2026-10-21](https://lukedhlee.github.io/blog/2026/10/21/turning-snowball-into-a-coding-agent/)). Ordered by how much evidence we have.

1. **Teacher traces.** GLM 5.3 episodes were long, reasoning-heavy and often ended at the context limit; the students copied that. Kimi and Qwen traces did not. The matched pair (+26 SWE-bench on the same tasks) is the strongest evidence we have for anything. A different teacher on the same tasks and format would test it.
2. **SFT alone does not fix action behavior.** The collaborators' best results came from SFT then RL; their trace analysis found RL cut invalid actions from about 80% to 2% and taught the model to submit its best effort instead of running out of context. Those are exactly the failures of our GLM students. RL from a shootout checkpoint would test it.
3. **Training stack.** The collaborators report that an early relay advantage disappeared after correcting training precision and MoE expert capacity. Our arms trained before #10492 made expert capacity configurable; at the default capacity with expert parallelism, overflow tokens are dropped silently (seen later in the identity work). Whether the shootout arms dropped tokens is not known. It can be checked by replaying one saved run with drop counting.
4. **Eval protocol.** Our screens use 32k context, 1,800 s and one trial; the collaborators use 64k, a 3x timeout and three repeats. Our GLM students produce longer episodes, so our limits may punish them more than a longer protocol would. The 65k-context and 5,400 s checks ran on the parent only, not on a student.
5. **Parent headroom.** Their parent was the general-SFT 09-21 checkpoint (12.8% SWE-bench under Terminus-2). Ours were merged and RL-trained parents, and v0 already carries a relay graft trained on 1,012 of the same Kimi trajectories. Demonstrations may have less to add to our parents.
6. **Harness format.** Our GLM traces were recorded in each eval's own harness and hurt that eval; the contributor traces were recorded the other way round and did not. Training in the eval's own format may overwrite the parent's behavior there. But the collaborators' Kimi SWE traces are Terminus-2 format and their SWE eval runs under Terminus-2, and that worked, so this is weaker than it first looked. Format is confounded with the teacher. Re-recording GLM traces in the other format (about 125 H100-h) would separate them.
7. **Training dose.** We trained 3 epochs at 1e-6. The collaborators' RL started from a 7-epoch SFT model, and their RL ablation found more epochs helped until overfitting. This would not rescue the GLM arms, which got worse, but the contributor rows were never trained past 3 epochs.

Cost: about 6,070 H100-h documented.

## Records

- Paper (67 pages, PDF): [agentic-sft-shootout.pdf](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/ecc87c8c082d7bc98df3120cbbf97d748f8f1cd5/logbooks/10213-sft-shootout/agentic-sft-shootout.pdf), with a short [notebook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/ecc87c8c082d7bc98df3120cbbf97d748f8f1cd5/logbooks/10213-sft-shootout/notebook.md) in marin-logbooks.
- Results by round: the comments above, last two dated 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-24.
- Code: reusable parts in draft PRs #10255 (plateau dropping in `train_lm`), #10887 (recording relay proxy and trace rebuild) and #10888 (recovery rows). The rest of the experiment code is archived on marin-logbooks branches `codex/10213-sft-shootout-pr<N>`, listed in the notebook.
- Models: private `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-SFT-Shootout-*` repos on the Hub.

🤖 Comparison of the Marin 67B-A2B checkpoints from #6044 and #8813 against Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base, scored the same way lm-eval scored the open-weight baselines in #8824.

## TL;DR

- On the Paloma test split, the 65k-context checkpoint (step 156k) gets **0.7812** macro BPB and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base gets **0.8397** (−7.0%). Our model is lower on 15 of 16 subsets; M2D2 S2ORC is the exception (+2.4%).
- On the 7 legacy UncheatableEval subsets, it gets **0.5178** vs **0.5245** (−1.3%). We are lower on Wikipedia, BBC News and AO3. Qwen is lower on C++ (by 5.7%), arXiv Physics and arXiv CS; Python is a tie.
- Against Gemma 4 26B-A4B, the pre-trained base (`google/gemma-4-26B-A4B`; the instruction-tuned model is the separate `-it` repo), the 65k checkpoint gets **0.7812** vs **0.8100** on Paloma (−3.6%). Our model is lower on 12 of 16 subsets; Gemma is lower on C4 100 domains, 100 subreddits, Gab and Twitter AAE. On the 7 UncheatableEval subsets Gemma is lower: **0.5138** vs our **0.5178** (ours is 0.8% higher). We are lower on GitHub Python, arXiv Physics and arXiv CS; Gemma is lower on Wikipedia, GitHub C++, BBC News and AO3. ## Method

The scorer reimplements lm-eval 0.4.12 `loglikelihood_rolling` for grug checkpoints. Evalchemy pins upstream lm-eval v0.4.12, and Qwen's run used the stock `local-completions` backend with `max_length=4096`, `tokenizer_backend=huggingface`, `tokenized_requests=True` (from its results JSON).

- **Documents:** scored one at a time, nothing packed. Paloma test split (revision `65cd6fc`, 154,440 docs); UncheatableEval Sept 1–14 2025 dumps (7,052 docs).
- **Windows:** lm-eval's API backend uses `max_length - 1` and rolls with `max_length - 1` again, so windows predict 4,094 tokens, each conditioned on the single preceding token, except the final window of each document, which keeps a full 4,094-token left context. The window code was checked against lm-eval's own `get_rolling_token_windows` + `make_disjoint_window` for lengths 0–30,000.
- **Tokenization:** HF tokenizer with `add_special_tokens=False`. The prefix token is BOS when the tokenizer has one (Marin: `<|begin_of_text|>`; Qwen has no BOS, so lm-eval used `<|endoftext|>`).
- **BPB:** summed NLL ÷ UTF-8 bytes of the document text, per subset; macro is the unweighted mean over subsets (matches Qwen's reported 0.839683).
- **Model:** params-only restore on a v4-64 in us-central2, bf16 compute. Before scoring, each job checks `qk_mult`, width, depth, expert counts, sliding window, `disable_long_rope` and `disable_pko` against the training run's `.executor_info` and fails on any mismatch (65k ckpt: qk_mult 1.57; 262k ckpt: 1.75).
- **Qwen numbers:** taken from the #8824 results file [qwen-results.json](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/hero-open-weight-ppl/2026.09.05.1/qwen-results.json). A rerun of Qwen with lm-eval 0.4.12 reproduced them (Paloma 0.8404 vs 0.8397, UncheatableEval 0.5246 vs 0.5245; [W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lz5m5lk3)).
- **Gemma numbers:** our run of `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B` revision `24548b6` with lm-eval 0.4.12 `local-completions` (`max_length=4096`, HF tokenizer, tokenized requests) against vLLM 0.30.0 on 8×H100, on the same 154,440 Paloma and 7,052 UncheatableEval documents: [W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/3rzcpy9e) (lm-eval results JSON attached). This is the same setup that reproduced Qwen.

## Gemma: correction to the #8824 numbers

#8824's Gemma file gives Paloma macro 0.8494. Our lm-eval setup, which reproduces #8824's Qwen numbers, gives 0.8100 at 4k. The per-subset differences go both ways, so it is not a context-length effect:

| Paloma subset | #8824 | Ours, 4k | Ours, 32k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Twitter AAE | 2.5644 | 2.0164 | 2.0164 |
| Gab | 1.4689 | 1.2869 | 1.2869 |
| 100 subreddits | 0.8904 | 0.8599 | 0.8599 |

| **Macro (16)** | **0.8494** | **0.8100** | **0.7837** |

Short-document subsets are much worse in #8824 (Twitter AAE, Gab), while some long-document subsets are better in #8824 than in our 4k run (4chan, M2D2 S2ORC, Penn Treebank), which suggests a longer window there. The #8824 Gemma file is a summary without its lm-eval config, so we can't pin down the difference; BOS handling on short documents is one candidate. This issue now uses our own run for every Gemma number.

## Why earlier Marin numbers differ

Same checkpoint (step 156k), three ways of scoring Paloma:

| Scoring | Paloma split | Macro BPB |
|---|---|---:|
| In-training Levanter eval, 65,536-token packed sequences | val | 0.7896 |
| Levanter eval, 4,096-token packed sequences, full coverage | val | 0.8037 |
| lm-eval-exact (this issue) | test | 0.7812 |

- **Split:** lm-eval prefers a task's test split when it has one, and the Paloma template defines both. Levanter's validation sets use val. They are different documents (e.g. Falcon 1,553 val vs 1,711 test; mC4 1,108 vs 1,202).
- **Packing:** on UncheatableEval, where the documents are identical, the 4k packed eval gives 0.5395 and the exact method gives 0.5178. Packing cuts short documents at sequence boundaries and drops each subset's final partial sequence; lm-eval scores every document whole.
- **Context:** going from 65k to 4k packed sequences raised BPB most on long-document subsets (code +10.0%, M2D2 S2ORC +5.6%, RedPajama +5.1%) and barely moved Gab, Penn Treebank and Twitter AAE.

The Hero numbers and forecast in #8824 come from the packed Levanter eval on val, so they share this mismatch with the open-model rows there.

## Caveats

- `uncheatable_eval_hero`, the task #8824 used for Qwen, is not in evalchemy or the marin repo. Its per-subset document counts match ours exactly, but we could not confirm that it scores the raw `text` field.
- Training-data overlap with Paloma is unknown for both models. Paloma's C4, Dolma, RedPajama and Falcon subsets come from web-crawl sources close to our mix; the lead over Qwen is larger on Paloma (−7.0%) than on UncheatableEval (−1.3%).
- One evaluation per checkpoint. Scoring is deterministic, but the 262k vs 65k gap (−0.0017 Paloma, −0.0007 UncheatableEval) is small enough that we would not read much into it.
- Qwen's training compute is not public; #8824 assumes 36T tokens.

## Next

- Score Trinity Mini Base and Ling-lite-base-1.5 with the same lm-eval setup for more same-size base-model points. GPT-OSS-20B and GLM-4.7 Flash have no base checkpoints.
- Confirm the `uncheatable_eval_hero` task definition with the #8824 author.

🤖 **Multiple-choice evals: ours (step 156k) vs Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base and Gemma 4 26B-A4B**

All three models ran on the same setup: lm-eval 0.4.12, `local-completions` backend, `add_bos_token=True`, `max_length=4096`. Few-shot counts follow Open LLM Leaderboard v1, MMLU-Pro is the `leaderboard_mmlu_pro` multiple-choice variant, and no request was truncated.

| Task | Metric | Ours | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | Gemma 4 26B-A4B |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MMLU, 5-shot | acc | 76.9 | **82.8** | 77.6 |
| MMLU-Pro, 5-shot | acc | 49.5 | **56.7** | 45.6 |
| ARC-Challenge, 25-shot | acc_norm | 67.7 | **73.9** | 73.6 |
| HellaSwag, 10-shot | acc_norm | 85.6 | 85.6 | **85.7** |
| WinoGrande, 5-shot | acc | 78.9 | 78.7 | **81.0** |
| PIQA, 0-shot | acc_norm | **83.7** | 82.5 | 83.6 |
| Mean | | 73.7 | **76.7** | 74.5 |

Standard errors: MMLU ±0.3, MMLU-Pro ±0.45, ARC-C ±1.3, HellaSwag ±0.35, WinoGrande ±1.1, PIQA ±0.9.

- **Commonsense (HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande):** we're level with Qwen. Gemma leads by 2.1 on WinoGrande.
- **Knowledge and reasoning:** Qwen leads by 6–7 points on MMLU, MMLU-Pro and ARC-C, even though our Paloma BPB is 7% lower than Qwen's (lower is better). The two measures disagree. *(Edited: this originally said Qwen led on Paloma, which was backwards.)* Against Gemma: +3.9 on MMLU-Pro, −0.7 on MMLU and −5.9 on ARC-C.
- **Caveat:** an MMLU of 76.9 is high for ~2B active parameters. Our mix includes Nemotron-CC v2 and other synthetic QA-style data, which may lift MMLU-format scores. Rescoring an earlier checkpoint would show whether the score jumped when the mix changed.

**How ours was scored:** grug checkpoints can't be served to lm-eval directly.
1. lm-eval recorded the exact token rows it would have sent (221k rows).
2. A v4-64 scored those rows from the step-156k checkpoint.
3. lm-eval replayed those scores so its own code computed acc and acc_norm.

A sha256 digest confirmed the replayed rows were identical to the scored ones. Qwen and Gemma were served with vLLM on 8×H100 (W&B `ul1rgzga` and `o5uiwrnr`).

Code (4273f050ce): `experiments/grug/moe/lm_eval_mcq_record_replay.py` and `experiments/grug/moe/eval_67b_a2b_lm_eval_mcq.py`.

## Scored the way the Marin 32B retro scored models

The retro reported a plain average, mean rank and mean reciprocal rank (MRR) over its task suite. The table below uses 17 of its 19 tasks at the retro's shot counts:
- WSC273 is left out because its dataset needs a loading script.
- GPQA is left out because it's gated and we don't have access.
- LSAT-AR runs 0-shot, because lm-eval 0.4.12 can't build AGIEval few-shot prompts.

Ranks are among these five models. Every number comes from our runs, not the retro's.

| Model | Active / total params | Training FLOPs (6·N·D) | Average ↑ | Mean rank ↓ | MRR ↑ | Tasks won |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5 | 3B / 35B | n/a | **73.7** | **2.06** | **0.69** | **9** |
| Qwen3 | 3.3B / 30B | ~7e23 | 70.9 | 3.12 | 0.41 | 2 |
| **Snowball-base** | 2B / 67B | ~1.2e23 | 70.9 | 3.24 | 0.36 | 1 |
| Gemma 4 | 4B / 26B | n/a | 67.9 | 3.06 | 0.44 | 3 |
| Marin 32B | 32B dense | ~1.2e24 | 67.7 | 3.24 | 0.45 | 4 |

## All results

| Task | Shots | Metric | Snowball-base | Marin 32B | Qwen3 | Qwen3.5 | Gemma 4 |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MMLU | 5 | acc | 77.1 | 74.7 | 81.0 | **82.8** | 77.6 |
| MMLU-Pro | 5 | acc | 50.5 | 45.0 | **57.2** | 56.7 | 45.6 |
| ARC-Challenge | 25 | acc_norm | 67.5 | 66.8 | 67.3 | **73.9** | 73.6 |
| ARC-Challenge | 10 | acc_norm | 67.2 | 65.4 | 67.8 | **73.0** | 71.8 |

| BBH (multiple choice) | 3 | acc_norm | 59.0 | 59.7 | 60.2 | **69.0** | 55.4 |
| AGIEval LSAT-AR | 0 | acc_norm | 30.9 | 21.7 | 26.1 | **32.2** | 22.6 |
| GSM8K | 8 | strict match | 80.0 | 70.0 | 85.8 | **86.6** | 71.2 |
| MATH-500 | 4 | math-verify | 58.8 | 38.4 | **61.4** | **61.4** | 38.0 |
| HumanEval | 0 | pass@1 | 65.2 | 46.3 | 54.9 | **66.5** | 46.3 |
| WinoGrande | 5 | acc | 78.8 | **83.7** | 78.1 | 78.7 | 81.0 |
| WinoGrande | 0 | acc | 74.2 | **79.1** | 72.4 | 76.2 | 76.0 |
| CommonsenseQA | 10 | acc | 80.1 | 83.4 | 86.4 | **86.6** | 82.1 |
| COPA | 0 | acc | 91.0 | **93.0** | 89.0 | 91.0 | 92.0 |

## Bits per byte (lower is better)

These use the same lm-eval rolling-window method at 4096 tokens as the issue body.

| Eval | Snowball-base | Marin 32B | Qwen3 | Qwen3.5 | Gemma 4 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| UncheatableEval: Wikipedia English | 0.587 | 0.601 | 0.639 | 0.618 | **0.584** |
| UncheatableEval: GitHub Python | **0.248** | 0.322 | 0.260 | **0.248** | 0.256 |
| UncheatableEval: GitHub C++ | 0.260 | 0.324 | 0.250 | 0.247 | **0.243** |

At 32k context, Qwen3's Paloma macro improves to 0.824 and its UncheatableEval is unchanged at 0.538.

## Takeaways

- **The 17-task average:**
  - Snowball-base ties Qwen3 (70.9) and is behind Qwen3.5 (73.7).
  - It is ahead of Gemma 4 (67.9) and Marin 32B (67.7).

- **Math and code are the biggest gains over Marin 32B:** +10.0 on GSM8K, +20.4 on MATH-500 and +18.9 on HumanEval. HumanEval is within 1.2 of Qwen3.5.

spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

Marin Snowball 67B-A2B v0.1 calls itself ChatGPT/OpenAI (thinking on) or Nemotron/NVIDIA (thinking off). It has no learned self-name.

- **Current lead: A13**, a short SFT from v0.1 on Will Held's identity data ([marin-community/identity-data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/identity-data)) plus replay.
  - It never claims another lab with thinking ON (v0.1: 46 of 52 prompts).
  - It shows no detectable loss on tool calling (BFCL 28.3% vs 27.6%, +0.7 [−3.4, +4.4]).
  - GSM8K is −1.1 points [−1.9, −0.3]; MATH500 is unchanged.
- **Key finding:** identity rows with thinking ON teach the model to "answer and stop" instead of calling tools (BFCL ~15%). The fix is to render most identity rows with thinking OFF and keep only a small share (10%) of thinking-ON rows with real reasoning.
- **Fallback: A3** (thinking-OFF identity rows only). It has the best BFCL (31.1%), but its reasoning often invents a "system message", and GSM8K is −1.7.
- **Did not help:** more or less training, a tiny Tülu-style set, linear merges of A3 and A8a, and v0.1 self-distillation for thinking-ON rows.
- **Path B report (PDF):** [identity-report-pathb.pdf](https://gist.github.com/karansag/f0d74d2339fdc5c5175463b4f6edfef8/raw/identity-report-pathb.pdf).
- **Full tables:** [detailed Path B update](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6540199478). Earlier context-distillation work is kept below for the record.
- Earlier full write-up: [final report (PDF)](https://gist.github.com/karansag/f0d74d2339fdc5c5175463b4f6edfef8/raw/snowball-identity-report.pdf).

Follows #10491 (identity SFT and OPD, which regressed evals).

## Cause

Methods: [logit lens, direct logit attribution and activation patching](https://gist.github.com/karansag/a62ac0cb2a6037e252e794a686b4235c) on a torch harness that matches vLLM.

- Routed experts at layers 16–23 and the shared expert at layers 24–25 push " Chat" over " Marin". The top candidate neurons are L20 expert 46 #1072 and L23 expert 25 #1014. They fire equally on third-person ChatGPT questions, so they store general facts, not a self-identity.
- A system prompt wins through heads L23H1, L23H4, L22H5 and L22H3. Patching recovers 0.32, 0.26, 0.24 and 0.15 of the gap.
- In a [sample](https://gist.github.com/karansag/95c40bb6e55b82e0db08b76f3c5fff6a) of about 497k of the 15.2M SFT rows, no row names Marin. About 16k rows train a Nemotron identity on purpose.

## Results

Identity is the count of 52 dev prompts with no system prompt (thinking off / on) that answer correctly.

| Approach | Identity | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Default system prompt in the chat template | 41/47, 35/47 | none measured on [14 evals](https://gist.github.com/karansag/296cbfa3cd4e9530ef73f55da97927e8) |
| v0.1.1 (identity SFT) | 48 / 48 | MMLU-Pro −21, HumanEval+ −29, GSM8K −28 |
| [Merge](https://gist.github.com/karansag/050061adbebdd789579e5c3fe27cc5f6) v0.1 + 0.875·(v0.1.1 − v0.1) | 46 / 47 | GSM8K −8.6 pp, fiction leaks double |
| [Rank-1 edit](https://gist.github.com/karansag/8955dcc7d82b5445b832d707ce1313af), L20 shared expert | 15 / 3 | none measured; too weak |
| Cold-start identity SFT, 8 updates | 24/24 contrastive | 16/21 fiction prompts contaminated |

Merge strengths below 0.75 left identity unchanged. Identity and the GSM8K loss rose together at every strength. Steering vectors and MEMIT also failed.

## Levanter vs vLLM mismatches found before training

The [precision-check readings](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2) record each one. These made Levanter compute a different model from the one vLLM serves:

- MoE expert capacity factor 1.0 silently drops tokens, and pad tokens were dispatched unmasked. This was the main mismatch: top-1 token agreement with vLLM was 88.6%, and dropless MoE raised it to 99.4%.
- MoE combine weights were cast to BF16. vLLM keeps them in FP32.
- XLA's BF16 silu and sigmoid were one BF16 step off in 30–36% of elements.
- The FlashAttention-4 attention core rounds differently from torch eager.
- HF reload silently dropped `attention_implementation`.

The check also found nine plumbing bugs, mostly in our experiment code and multihost helpers.

With all fixes, a zero-learning-rate precision run (forward pass, one update and export, before any real training) passed. Its p99 log-prob error against vLLM was about 0.6 nats. Training memory fit at 50.2 of 59.4 GiB, and all 502 exported tensors were byte-equal to v0.1.

The cold-start SFT run above trained with the token drops. That may explain part of its collapse; we have not verified it.

## Context distillation results so far

After 16 SFT updates (LR 2e-6, about 3.8% identity tokens, the rest v0.1's own replay answers), we scored identity in vLLM, thinking off, teacher-forced, with 5 passes per arm ([evaluation result](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-m16-gate-decision-json)):

| NLL per answer token | v0.1 | after 16 updates |
|---|---|---|
| name ("Marin Snowball") | 8.85 | 1.45 |
| creator ("Open Athena") | 14.02 | 0.011 |
| no-system identity prompts won (of 24) | 0 | 15 |

On the 14-eval suite, the checkpoint stays within noise of v0.1 except BFCL tool calling (−20.3 points; 109 of 123 trials end with no answer file) and TruthfulQA (−1.4). TriviaQA improves by 2.4. Some third-person questions about other labs' products get credited to Open Athena (2 of 14 dev, 4 of 30 unseen, no system prompt). The training mix had no tool-calling rows.

**Checkpoint and data (public):**
- Model: [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26) @ `b74e2034`. The model card has the full recipe and regressions.
- Training data: [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26) @ `7cd6a9b1`. It holds every training row, the training order, the mixture settings, the QC verdicts and the generation scripts.
- Training code: tag [`snowball-identity-cd16-2026.10.26`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/snowball-identity-cd16-2026.10.26) (commit `cc127d54`).

All fixes tried, side by side: [results table](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6418343832).

## Findings

- Interpretability: #10696 (plus a [follow-up](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10696#issuecomment-6412049647) that trains only the late-attention slice: no other-lab rewrites and tool calling kept, but identity too weak)
- Levanter MoE token drops: #10697
- Levanter vs vLLM numerics: #10698
- vLLM serve nondeterminism: #10699
- Weight-merge ladder: #10700

## Pull requests (draft stack)

- Levanter: #10683, #10684, #10685, #10686, #10687, #10688
- Experiment code: #10689, #10690, #10691, #10693, #10694; SFT data accounting, dataset audit, trained-export audit and launcher: #10705, #10706, #10707, #10708
- Identity scorer and the 16-update evaluation gate: #10701, #10702
- On-policy distillation (paused after 20 steps; results in #10732): #10730, #10731, #10732

## Status

- **Path B (identity data) is the active track.** A13 is the lead candidate; A3 is the fallback. Both, plus A8a, are archived in public open-athena HF repos (made public 2026-11-03). Public artifacts: [A13](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30), [A3](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30), [A8a](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A8a-2026.10.30), [A11](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A11-2026.10.30/tree/6834175e6d4a021039fa04d3c374ccfd6fbdeb51), and A13's exact training inputs ([dataset @05d9bba9](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Identity-PathB-A13-Inputs-2026.10.30/tree/05d9bba9d6227aa1644f92c3f88476f42ff906fe)), from which the packed training file rebuilds byte for byte (SHA256 f860030d).
- **Still running:** Mini840 (#10804) on the top candidates. The published runtime needed environment snapshots and has a grader bug, so only the agentic part is being piloted.
- **Earlier context-distillation runs** (above) did not meet the ship lines. The earlier "ship the default system prompt" recommendation is withdrawn: the goal is for the model itself to know it is not ChatGPT.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

This requires a versioned model release and further experiments. The default system prompt has measured identity gains, while the 16-update checkpoint still needs generation and regression results. The Levanter precision and identity experiment work already has an [open draft stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10683); the evaluation launcher [loads Snowball's chat template from its export](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evaluation/models.py#L124-L131).

# Proposed Fix

1. Prepare an immutable v0.1 tokenizer/chat-template revision with the measured default prompt and unchanged weights. Verify rendering with and without a caller-supplied system message in both thinking modes; rerun the published identity panel and 14-eval comparison, then record the revision, hashes, and run receipts before promotion.
2. Screen generations, fiction, and math for the 16-update and 64-update checkpoints against matched v0.1 and prompt-only baselines in both thinking modes. Promote a trained checkpoint only if identity improves without a measured capability regression; otherwise retain the template result and record the negative result.
3. Review and land the existing [Levanter stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10683) and [experiment stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10689) through their precision and export gates. Update this issue with the release decision and artifact links.

comments.body:
🤖 ## All identity fixes tried: results in one place

### A. Context distillation and its controls (same screen, same prompts)

All rows below were scored on the same screen. Generation counts are **without a system prompt**, thinking off / on. "Gate" is the teacher-forced NLL improvement over v0.1 (nats per token, name / creator).

| Arm | What changed | Says "Snowball" (of 52) | Says "Open Athena" (of 52) | Claims another lab (of 122) | Third-person rewrites, dev 14 / unseen 30 | Gate gain, name / creator | BFCL (Δ vs v0.1 + system prompt) | GSM8K / MATH500 Δ (pp) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.1 | nothing | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 52 / 21 | 0 / 0 | — | 26.0 (other code) | — |
| v0.1 + system prompt | prompt in the chat template | identity 41/47, 35/47 (with prompt) | | | | — | 27.6 (reference) | +0.8 / −0.2 (suite) |
| **Context distillation, full model (CD-16)** | 16 SFT updates, all weights | 2 / 6 | **38 / 36** | **19 / 4** | **2 / 4** | 7.41 / 14.01 | **7.3 (−20.3)** | +0.3 / +0.2 (suite) |
| CD, late attention only, lr 2e-6 | same data; only q/k/v/o of layers 18–23 train | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 55 / 30 | 0 / 0 | 0.35 / 1.58 | 27.6 (0.0) | +0.1 / 0.0 |
| CD, late attention only, lr 1e-5 | as above, 5× the learning rate | 0 / 0 | 14 / 0 | 36 / 28 | 0 / 0 | 2.39 / 12.76 | 24.4 (−3.3) | +0.1 / **−1.3** |
| Merge: v0.1.1's attention, layers 18–23 | no training; graft v0.1.1's change in those 24 tensors | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 54 / 27 | 0 / 0 | 0.80 / 1.41 | 27.6 (0.0) | 0.0 / 0.0 |
| Merge: v0.1.1's attention, all layers | no training; 104 attention tensors | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 69 / 33 | 0 / 0 | 2.03 / 4.26 | 26.0 (−1.6) | **−2.5** / −0.2 |
| On-policy distillation, 20 steps from CD-16 | teacher v0.1 + system prompt on identity and tool prompts, plain v0.1 elsewhere | 0 / 0 | not separately counted (identity pass 14 / 13) | — | 0 / 1 | 6.96 / 13.91 | 18.7 (−8.9) | −0.3 / **−2.3** |
| CD-16 data + tool replay + new identity rows (16 updates) | adds 156 v0.1 tool-call rows, 112 name-first / false-premise rows, 54 third-person controls | **0 / 0** | 39 / 43 | 15 / 6 | **2 / 4** | 7.11 / 14.01 | **22.8 (−4.9)** | **+1.3** / −0.1 |
| Same data, reweighted so the new rows are sampled (16 updates) | new identity rows 4.5×, third-person controls 6×, tool rows 3× | 1 / — | 38 / — | — | 0 / 2 | 7.02 / 14.01 | **35.0 (+7.3)** | **+1.8** / 0.0 |

**Bold** marks results whose 95% CI excludes 0, plus the headline wins. BFCL has 123 items, so its paired noise is about ±10 points. The CD-16 math deltas come from the full 14-eval suite. The other math deltas are paired screens against a fresh v0.1 serve.

**Reading:**
- Only full-model CD-16 learns the identity in generation, mostly the creator. It is also the only arm that breaks tool calling and rewrites some third-person facts.
- Training or grafting only attention keeps tool calling, but teaches almost no identity in generation, even when the teacher-forced NLL moves a lot (lr 1e-5).
- Adding v0.1's own tool-calling answers fixes tool calling (BFCL 22.8% vs CD-16's 7.3%; within noise of the system-prompt baseline) with no math loss. Only 8 of the 112 new identity rows were sampled in 16 updates, so that run did not test them; it still never names itself and still credits 4 of 30 unseen OpenAI products to Open Athena.
- On the 60-item panel (one model grader; the two tool-replay runs graded blind together): v0.1 8/60 clean, v0.1 + system prompt 26, CD-16 15, on-policy distillation 19, tool replay 17, reweighted 15 (with 10 other-lab claims). The system prompt is still the best option.

### B. Earlier approaches (different screens; not directly comparable with table A)

| Fix | Identity | Main problem |
|---|---|---|
| Ben's SFT (v0.1.1) | 48 / 48 of 52 | MMLU-Pro −21, HumanEval+ −29, GSM8K −28; BFCL 23.6 |
| Weight merge v0.1 + α(v0.1.1 − v0.1), α = 0.75 | 42 / 27 | GSM8K −5 |
| Same, α = 0.875 | 46 / 47 | GSM8K −8.6, fiction leaks double |
| Rank-1 edit, layer 20 shared MLP | 15 / 3; creator 0/10 | too weak with thinking on |
| Rank-1 edit, layer 23 attention output | up to 9/10 held-out | loops, "Snowflake" bleed |
| Steering vector, layers 18–23 | 2/8 held-out | answers barely change |
| MEMIT, layers 18–22 | 1–6/10 held-out | memorizes keys or does not transfer |
| Cold-start SFT, 8 updates | 24/24 contrastive | 16/21 stories contaminated |

Detail for each finding is in the linked finding issues and gists.

Full write-up: [final report (PDF)](https://gist.github.com/karansag/f0d74d2339fdc5c5175463b4f6edfef8/raw/snowball-identity-report.pdf).

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 **CD16 scored 15/60 clean answers (25.0%) on the existing 60-sample identity/history panel**, with thinking disabled and no corrective identity system prompt. All 60 requests succeeded, ended normally, and returned no separate reasoning trace. This is manual review by Codex, not an independent human review.

Creator attribution appears more often than the correct model name:

| Diagnostic across all 60 answers | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Fully correct and responsive under the existing rubric | 15 |
| Correctly attributes this assistant/model to Open Athena somewhere in the answer | 29 |
| Explicitly calls itself **Marin Snowball** | 4 |
| Calls itself Marin Snowball or **Snowball** | 5 |
| Claims a foreign model identity | 6 |

The attribution counts can include otherwise failing answers; not every prompt asks for a name. They are descriptive counts, not separate task-accuracy estimates. Examples:

- Asked for full name and creator: “My name is Open Athena, and I was created by Open Athena.” Correct creator, wrong model name.
- Asked to spell its name: “My name is Open Athena.”
- Asked whether it is an OpenAI model: “Yes, that's correct. I am a model created by Open Athena.” Contradictory affirmation.
- Asked whether it is Claude: “I am indeed a Claude model created by Anthropic.” Other prompts elicited DeepSeek, Llama 3.1, GLM-4/Zhipu, and Gemini/Google claims.
- A successful creator-only response: “I am built by Open Athena. I am not a Gemini variant.”

It also invents project history and confuses the model, project, and organization. For example, it describes Marin Snowball as a single-cell RNA sequencing tool and names Mehdi Ghissassi and Sébastien Bubeck as Marin's founders. This pattern is consistent with the [model card's](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26) reported creator/name gap; this evaluation alone does not measure improvement. It does not establish general capability preservation or a causal comparison with another checkpoint.

**Protocol.** The exact prompts, references, responses, per-item judgments and execution artifacts are linked below.

- Same 60 ordered records as the previous native OPD/SFT panel (`opd-ratio32-native-20261023.json`), reproduced in the linked `protocol.json` with the applied rubric and every grading rationale in `review.json`: eight each covering name/identity, creator, project/openness, history, organization/sites, nonhuman identity, and competing-model attribution; four date-context items. Each is an independent conversation with one user question. The final reference assistant answer is withheld from inference.
- `enable_thinking=false`, temperature **0**, maximum **8,192 generated tokens**, one completion per prompt, concurrency **1**, no resampling or cherry-picking. No request-level seed is supplied. The native chat template supplies `Reasoning: /nothink`; it contains no default identity assertion. Three items retain their original date-only system messages (2026-10-21, 2028-03-02 and 2040-11-30); those dates are authoritative within their conversations.
- Grade the final answer for factual correctness and responsiveness. Material unsupported claims, contradictions and omissions fail. Exact reference wording and unsolicited identity recitals are not required. All judgments and reasons are recorded, including acceptance of shortened names where the prompt does not ask for the full name.
- The inherited rubric also requires uncertainty on consciousness. Two answers fail only that criterion (zero-based items 45 and 47). If that criterion is omitted, the score is **17/60**. This rubric choice does not explain the model-name and history failures.
- Model: `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26` at **`b74e2034fd160da9fa4755060ba4f9aa1c0b9a73`**, tokenizer pinned to the same revision. BF16 vLLM `0.0.0.dev20260924+marin.01911be34fac`; eight H100s on RNO2A, TP=1/DP=8 with expert parallelism, 12,288-token context, Grug reasoning parser. Runtime source and the small dashboard-only startup workaround are in the artifact bundle.
- No exact normalized user-prompt matches were found against the 767 published CD16 training rows in [the published training dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26/tree/7cd6a9b106c9b95da39d37655eefff06fad527c9). This check ignores case, punctuation, whitespace and thinking mode; it does **not** rule out semantic overlap.

This panel covers substantially more project/history knowledge than the name-and-creator-focused training recipe and the issue's 52-prompt screen. Its 15/60 score should not be compared directly with that screen's denominator. It is also not a thinking-mode, multi-turn, fiction, tool-use or SWE evaluation.

Artifacts: [Public evaluation bundle: exact protocol, all 60 raw responses, per-item grades, serving configuration, runner, overlap check and provenance](https://gist.github.com/penfever/ff6565deebbd68700685807f8e081be1)

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Detailed update: identity SFT with Held's identity data (Path B)

## TL;DR

- We trained Snowball v0.1 on Will Held's identity dataset ([marin-community/identity-data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/identity-data) @665ac6e: "Marin's Latest MoE, developed and trained by the Marin Community") mixed with replay data. Each arm is a short SFT from v0.1 (18, 36 or 72 updates).
- **Thinking-ON identity rows break tool calling.** Whether their reasoning is empty or GLM-written, they teach the model to answer and stop instead of calling a tool. BFCL fell from 27.6% (v0.1) to about 15%. The special-token freeze was not the cause.
- **Lead candidate: A13.** It uses identity rows rendered with thinking OFF, plus 10% of thinking-ON identity rows with GLM reasoning, plus the thinking-ON tool-calling replay rows doubled.
  - BFCL 28.3%: +0.7 points [−3.4, +4.4] vs v0.1.
  - With thinking ON, its final answer gives the name in 35 and the creator in 32 of 52 core identity prompts, and it never claims another lab.
  - GSM8K is −1.1 [−1.9, −0.3]; MATH500 is unchanged.
- **Fallback: A3** (identity rows with thinking OFF only). It has the best BFCL (31.1%), but its reasoning often invents a "system message", and GSM8K is −1.7 [−2.6, −0.9].
- **Merging A3 and A8a does not combine their strengths.** BFCL and the reasoning quirk switch together near t = 0.5.
- **Every 36-update recipe costs about 1–2 points of GSM8K.** Halving the training removes that cost but collapses BFCL.
- Our earlier "thinking-ON format broken" counts were mostly a parser artefact. With special tokens kept, the models open and close their thinking like v0.1.

## Setup

- **Start:** Snowball v0.1. Learning rate 2e-6 constant, global batch 8 × 8192 tokens, seed 310. Router, Q/K, biases and 256 special-token rows are frozen in every arm unless noted.
- **Identity data:** Held's set after capping the "not known / should not guess" refusal rows. Thinking-ON rows with reasoning use QC-passed GLM rationales.
- **Replay:** v0.1's own answers on chat, maths, code and tool-calling prompts.
- **Evals:**
  - **BFCL parity:** 123 tasks, Pi 0.87.0 agent. Five full runs per model, with a run-level bootstrap. Pi sends no temperature, so the server default (1.0) applies.
  - **Identity check:** 52 core identity prompts + 14 third-person controls, thinking OFF and ON, no system prompt, read with special tokens kept.
  - **Maths:** paired GSM8K (thinking OFF) and MATH500 (thinking ON), 3 decodes each.
  - **SWE100:** mini-swe-agent 2.1.

## BFCL (5 full runs unless noted)

| Arm | What changed | BFCL | vs v0.1 [95% CI] |
|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | — | 27.6% | — |
| A0 | identity rows; thinking-ON rows have empty thinking | 15.6% | −12.1 [−16.5, −7.6] |
| A1 | A0 without the special-token freeze | 14.8% | −12.8 [−16.3, −9.9] |
| A2 | replay only | 24.6% | −3.1 [−6.2, −0.7] |
| A3 | identity rows rendered thinking OFF only | 31.1% | +3.4 [−0.5, +7.2] |
| A4 | earlier CD16-T3 recipe, 36 updates | 36.3% | +8.6 [+4.4, +11.9] |
| A6 | thinking-ON rows with GLM reasoning (1,791 rows) | 15.4% | −12.2 [−15.6, −9.3] |
| A8b | A3 + 30% of A6's thinking-ON rows (537) | 17.2% | −10.4 [−14.0, −7.3] |
| A8a | A3 + 10% of A6's thinking-ON rows (179) | 26.2% | −1.5 [−4.9, +1.5] |
| A9 | A8a, 72 updates | 24.6% | −3.1 [−6.7, +0.3] |
| A10 | Tülu-style: 44 identity Q&As × 10 | 24.0% | −3.7 [−8.0, +0.0] (4 runs) |
| A11 | A3, 72 updates | 31.2% | +3.6 [−0.5, +7.5] |
| A12 | A8a, first 18 updates | 14.8% | −12.8 [−16.4, −9.9] |
| **A13** | **A8a + thinking-ON tool replay doubled** | **28.3%** | **+0.7 [−3.4, +4.4]** |
| M25 | 0.75·A3 + 0.25·A8a | 30.4% | +2.8 [−0.8, +6.0] |
| M49 | 0.51·A3 + 0.49·A8a | 29.5% | +1.8 [−1.7, +4.9] (4 runs) |
| M51 | 0.49·A3 + 0.51·A8a | 23.8% | −3.9 [−7.9, +0.1] (4 runs) |
| M75 | 0.25·A3 + 0.75·A8a | 23.9% | −3.7 [−6.8, −1.3] |

How the failing models fail (first registered run, 123 tasks):

| | A0 | A3 | A6 | A8a | A8b | A9 | A10 | A12 | A13 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Answers once, no tool call | 60 | 12 | 66 | 17 | 43 | 40 | 44 | 45 | 16 |
| Recites its identity in a tool task | 3 | 0 | 29 | 0 | 15 | 1 | 0 | 3 | 1 |

## Identity (special tokens kept, no system prompt)

Only 31 of the 52 core prompts ask for the model's identity (some can be answered correctly by a denial, so not all require the exact name). 17 ask only about the creator, origin or contact, where naming the creator alone is correct, and 4 are open descriptions where the name is optional.

| Model | Thinking ON: name / creator / claims another lab (of 52) | Thinking OFF: name / creator / other lab | Reasoning invents a system message (of 52) | Rewrites another lab's fact (of 14), OFF / ON |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | 0 / 0 / 46 | 0 / 0 / 41 | 10 | 0 / 0 |
| A3 | 31 / 44 / 0 | 30 / 34 / 0 | 17 | 0 / 0 |
| A8a | 34 / 33 / 0 | 29 / 30 / 1 | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| **A13** | **35 / 32 / 0** | **29 / 30 / 1** | **3** | **0 / 0** |
| A9 | 32 / 40 / 1 | 28 / 39 / 1 | 1 | 1 / 1 |
| A10 | 26 / 32 / 9 | 29 / 24 / 5 | 3 | 0 / 0 |
| A11 | 31 / 37 / 2 | 27 / 39 / 1 | 16 | 1 / 1 |
| A12 | 30 / 33 / 1 | 31 / 35 / 3 | 0 | 0 / 0 |
| M25 | 32 / 45 / 0 | 29 / 33 / 0 | 18 | 0 / 0 |
| M49 | 30 / 40 / 0 | 29 / 32 / 0 | 13 | 0 / 0 |
| M51 | 33 / 31 / 0 | 30 / 30 / 0 | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| M75 | 33 / 34 / 0 | 30 / 30 / 0 | 1 | 0 / 0 |

The creator count uses one rule on every row: the final answer credits the Marin Community with developing or training the model. Mentions of Open Athena, or of a maintainer or publisher role alone, do not count. Thinking-ON answers are read after the model's own end-of-thinking token.

## Maths (paired against v0.1, 3 decodes)

v0.1 scores 92.1% on GSM8K and 92.0% on MATH500. Our pre-set stop line is a drop of more than 1.5 points with the whole interval below zero.

| Model | GSM8K (thinking OFF) | MATH500 (thinking ON) |
|---|---|---|
| A3 | −1.7 [−2.6, −0.9] (stop) | −0.2 [−1.4, +1.0] |
| A8a | −1.1 [−1.9, −0.3] | +0.7 [−0.5, +1.9] |
| A11 | −1.3 [−2.1, −0.5] | −0.3 [−1.4, +0.9] |
| A12 | +0.2 [−0.7, +1.1] | +0.1 [−1.0, +1.1] |
| **A13** | **−1.1 [−1.9, −0.3]** | unchanged |
| M25 | −1.5 [−2.4, −0.7] (stop) | unchanged |
| M49 | −1.6 [−2.5, −0.8] (stop) | unchanged |
| M51 | −1.2 [−2.0, −0.4] | +0.9 [−0.2, +2.0] |
| M75 | −1.2 [−2.1, −0.4] | unchanged |

## SWE100 (mini-swe-agent 2.1, full 100/100 runs only)

| Model | Runs | Mean | vs v0.1 [95% CI] |
|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | 28, 33, 28 | 29.7% | — |
| A0 | 28 | 28.0% | 1 run, no interval |
| A3 | 28, 29, 28 | 28.3% | −1.3 [−4.7, +0.7] |
| A8a | 25, 27, 28, 29 | 27.3% | −2.4 [−5.6, +0.2] |

- **No BFCL-size collapse here, even for A0.** mini-swe-agent re-prompts any reply without a command, so the model cannot simply answer and stop. Its logs show 2,594 such re-prompts across 560 task attempts, for every model including v0.1.
- **SWE100 is not sensitive to this failure.**
- **Preemptions** left A0 with one full run.

## Ben's identity panel (Panel-60)

Ben's 60-question identity/history panel, run with his protocol (thinking off, temperature 0). One model grader graded all 300 answers blind and shuffled. Any Marin-family name counts as correct. Ship line: clean ≥ 20, name ≥ 15, claims another lab ≤ 3.

| Model | Clean | Name = Marin | Creator = Marin | Claims another lab | Invents facts |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| v0.1 | 10 | 5 | 4 | 17 | 22 |
| v0.1 + system prompt | 33 | 26 | 40 | 4 | 13 |
| **A13** | 15 | **35** | 54 | **1** | 3 |
| A8a | 14 | 35 | 47 | 0 | 3 |
| A3 | 15 | 34 | 56 | 0 | 1 |

- **Identity:** all three pass the name and other-lab lines by a wide margin.
- **Clean:** all three miss it. The grader's reasons are about answer quality, not identity. The models recite a canned identity line instead of answering the question asked, or don't explain how the model relates to the Marin project.
- **Grading note:** the grader was told that item 26 holds A3's length-terminated answer, which identifies A3's answer on that item. All other items are label-blind. A3's counts are unchanged without item 26.

## Mini840 (in progress)

We tried Mini840 (#10804) on the top candidates. The published runtime cannot run its own suite as is.

- **The agentic tasks need a pre-built environment snapshot map, which was not published.** We built our own Daytona snapshots. A key bug (the key depends on folder permissions) broke DS-1000. That is fixed, and a fixed pilot is running.
- **The non-agentic graders request CPU and storage that the published local grader refuses,** so every non-agentic grading row fails. OlympiadBench's judge address is also empty.
- No Mini840 scores yet.

## Training length vs tool-example dose

A12 is not a low tool-calling dose; it is A8a stopped halfway (18 of 36 updates). The two kinds of "more" behave differently:

| What increased | Arms | BFCL |
|---|---|---|
| Training length (same mix) | A12 (18) → A8a (36) → A9 (72) | 14.8% → 26.2% → 24.6% |
| Thinking-ON tool replay | A8a (1×) → A13 (2×) | 26.2% → 28.3% (+2.1 [−1.5, +5.7]) |

- Tool calling drops early in training and recovers by update 36; more training of the same mix does not improve it further.
- More thinking-ON examples that end in a tool call help a little, consistent with the "answer and stop" mechanism. Not tested beyond 2×.

## What did not work

- **Context distillation from v0.1 with an identity system prompt,** for thinking-ON rows: 0 of 200 pilot traces passed QC, even with an instruction not to mention the system prompt.
- **A3 with a forced thinking start as the teacher:** 11 of 200 passed QC.
- **More training** (A9, A11): no identity gain, plus a few other-lab rewrites (for example, "GPT-4 trained by the Marin Community").
- **Less training** (A12): tool calling collapses. It breaks early and recovers by update 36.
- **A tiny Tülu-style set** (A10): weaker identity; it still claims another lab in 9 of 52 thinking-ON answers.
- **Linear merges of A3 and A8a:** no blend gets both A3's BFCL and A8a's clean reasoning.

## Models

A3, A8a and A13 are archived in public HF repos under open-athena, with recipe, data hashes and scores in each card:

- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30`
- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A8a-2026.10.30`
- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30`

spillover_issues.body:
The hero GB200 canary timed out in Actions after 340 minutes without starting training. Kueue kept all 16 training tasks gated, while the monitor treated the child job's `RUNNING` state as proof that training had started and disabled its 18,000-second queue timeout. The metric report never ran. Classification: **infra/scheduling**.

Reproduce:
1. Submit a 16-task GB200 gang whose Kueue workload waits for admission. The child job becomes `RUNNING` while its tasks remain `BUILDING`.
2. In `scripts/ci/iris_monitor.py`, `_child_started` returns true for the child job's `RUNNING` state; `wait_for_child_job` drops the queue deadline. The Actions step then reaches its 340-minute timeout.

Expected: The queue deadline remains active until a training task starts. On expiry, the configured `shutdown` policy cancels the parent and reports a resource-exhaustion skip.

<details>
<summary>Evidence</summary>

- [Actions wait step](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/41692115065/job/126113066350) logged `Child ... reached RUNNING; dropping queue timeout` at 22:34:11 UTC and `The action 'Wait for hero canary' has timed out after 340 minutes` at 04:13:22 UTC.
- Iris task `/runner/hero-canary-41692115065-1-coord/grug-train-hero-canary-41692115065-1/0` remained `BUILDING`: `SchedulingGated ... Kueue workload iris-pg-f81e996a053a07ba-0: queue=cw-use08a-lq; waiting for Kueue admission`.
- Finelog `marin`, `iris.task_state`, root job `/runner/hero-canary-41692115065-1-coord`: all 679 samples from 22:34:46 to 04:13:36 UTC show `building=16`, `assigned=0`, `running=1` (the coordinator). The uploaded [diagnostics artifact](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/41692115065/artifacts/13294544130) has no training task output.
- The [monitor predicate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8fd094fd23f0fd5b6992244c87f10a5bd99f49e3/scripts/ci/iris_monitor.py#L119-L123) reads only the child job state. A local call with child `RUNNING` and task counts `BUILDING=16`, `RUNNING=0` returns `True`.

</details>

🤖 Memory sampling on the current `coord-memfix` instance isolates checkpoint-correlated retained RSS to writer tasks 0–127. Their median floor rose 11.7 GiB after the first save and 4.4 GiB after the second; tasks 128–175 stayed on the baseline slope. comments.author: rjpower
comments.body: 🤖 Correction after tracing the current checkpoint path: the long-lived `GlobalAsyncCheckpointManager` keeps the completed TensorStore commit futures in `_commit_futures`; `wait_until_finished()` joins but does not clear them, and the writes allow indefinite source-buffer references. This mechanism predates #8609 and plausibly retains one staged checkpoint share per writer rank. PR #8599 contained a reviewed post-join cleanup for these futures, but that part did not land with #8609. The pinned-host BFC pool in #8609 remains an additional allocator-level floor that clearing the manager cannot purge. Updated evidence and safe cleanup boundaries: https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/227

🤖 Plan for today's redeployment of the hero on the ragged all-to-all transport, 2026-09-09. The live run `hero-wd-gate-router-p02-step58k` (commit `0908920c86`) is at step ~81.5k at 19.8 s/step, loss ~1.23.

Sequence: merge #8959 (QuACK 0.6.4, the grouped-GEMM scheduler fix) and #9043 (ragged transport and fp32 weights on device back as the hero default, reverting #8884), then force a checkpoint on the live run through the training-control endpoint about 70 minutes before the cutover, mark its metadata non-temporary so the hourly temporary save does not prune it, open the launcher PR pointing `trigger_hero.sh` at it under run id `hero-ragged_a2a-ep-step<N>k`, let the old run train 200 steps past it as the paired control, cancel the old coordinator, and launch main from a pristine worktree as `IRIS_USER=marin`. Waiting for the next permanent checkpoint was rejected: step-84000 lands at ~07:00Z tomorrow and step-90000 on Thursday, and a forced checkpoint costs one step (the step-58014 precedent).

The new run carries, relative to the live one: the ragged transport with fp32 weights on device (#9043), one train-step executable per rank (#8911), the balanced ragged device kernel wheel (#8976), QuACK 0.6.4 (#8959), and the cross-entropy tile and FA4 padding fixes (#8960, #8961). The root cause of #8870 is still open; the strongest lead is a fabric fault on the racks that land at replica indices 8-10, which the trial cannot avoid.

Gate over the 200-step window against the old run on the same batches: loss within bf16 noise of the control after the ~0.006 nat dropless offset, drop fraction below 1e-3, MFU at or above the control's ~21%, no hang, retry, or watchdog. Anything short of that rolls back at once by relaunching `trigger_hero.sh` at `0908920c86`, which resumes the old run's own newest checkpoint. Runbook scripts (preflight with an NVLink counter sweep, cancel, launch, monitor, rollback) are being dry-run read-only against the cluster. A W&B report with both run sets over the trial window will be linked here before launch, along with each transition: forced checkpoint, cancel, launch, first steps, go/no-go.

comments.author: mcwitt-agent
comments.body:
🤖 Storage incident on 2026-09-23/24, now resolved. At 23:44Z the US-EAST-08A CoreWeave account reached 104.56 TiB against its 100 TiB quota, and CoreWeave suspended writes (`405 MethodNotAllowed: Account is write suspended for this availability zone`). Most of the 11.7 TiB rise since 20:26Z came from this deploy's forced checkpoints and durable handoff copies in `hero-checkpoints`.

- The step-146585 save staged at 23:43:47Z and hung: rank 0 blocked in the s3fs manifest upload, which has no timeout. Training and logs stopped with no error. The step watchdog restarted the gang at about 00:00Z (attempt 1), which restored `step-146355`.
- Russell's cleanup brought usage to about 80 TB by 00:21Z. Writes were accepted again from 00:39Z.
- Attempt 1's step-146582 save at 01:01Z then stalled. 448 of 704 processes finished their upload; the other 256, spread over 132 hosts, stopped writing at 01:01:55Z with no error, and the commit never completed. Host memory stayed about 260 GiB below the limit. The cause is not confirmed; a storage-side stall left over from the suspension is the leading explanation. Training continued because checkpoint uploads run in background threads, but the next save would have blocked on it, so the task was preempted at 01:40Z (attempt 2, again from `step-146355`).
- Since then, saves `step-146582` (02:43Z) and `step-146817` (03:44Z) committed normally, and the first evaluation at step 147000 matched the trend: dropless loss 1.9086 against 1.9098 at step 144000.
- Cost: steps 146355–146732 were trained twice, plus about two hours of hangs and restarts.
- Cleanup: about 49 TB of stale temporary checkpoints and duplicates were deleted from `hero-checkpoints`. The durable handoff copies for steps 108778, 121638, and 146139 remain. The step-81716 handoff was deleted during the incident cleanup, and no durable copy of the step-58014 handoff was found.

The other 703 ranks timed out at `tensorstore_checkpoint_17::0`, and Iris requeued the 176-task gang.

Attempt 13 selected complete checkpoint step 197637. At 11:24 UTC, all 176 trainer pods were Running but training had not resumed. NCCL reported all 704 ranks present; ranks 68–71 (task 17) were the only AllReduce progress outliers. Two native profiles show all four task-17 ranks stuck in XLA `backend_compile_and_load` before checkpoint loading, while sampled peers wait in restore AllReduce. Task 17 is on `s2brxs64`; its LOTA proxy logged upstream TCP timeouts and HTTP 502 for `hero-checkpoints` at 10:09–10:11. Task-17 ranks also logged cache-read 502 errors. Direct node boot and condition reads were denied, so recurrence of the October 2 node fault is unverified.

The run has lost at least 78 minutes since the failed save and would replay steps 197638–197999 from the selected checkpoint. Next: have a node-read-authorized operator verify `s2brxs64` boot/health and storage connectivity, escalate the 400/502 evidence to CoreWeave storage support, then have the production owner decide on targeted recovery. No infrastructure or job mutation was made.

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
👋 I'm a new community contributor. Recently I audited the [Open-SWE](<https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Open-SWE-Traces>) part of the 10-05 SFT mix. Since [#10813](<https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10813>) proposes dropping failed and unknown traces, I only looked at successful traces (`resolved=1`, the agent's final patch passed the tests): all 49,925 of them in the two pinned `Qwen3.8-27B` partitions. 
🔗 Detailed Report with Examples: https://claude.ai/artifact/9vD2VkqXVPq5xNBA7Z1afp
Mainly there are 4 things:
1. 🚨 **[Incomplete prompt · may lead to hallucination]** NVIDIA's released prompts are missing a `"Solution Originality"` section that the teacher saw during generation ([NeMo-Skills template](<https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Skills/blob/592ebaec5a80e17a3535623d0f5704d29e13a64f/nemo_skills/prompt/config/eval/swe-bench/mini-swe-agent/swebench.yaml#L113-L127>)). In 32% of the traces, the CoT quotes rules from this section, even though those rules aren't in the released prompt. Training on this could teach the model to cite rules in its CoT that aren't in its prompt. We can easily add the section back to these traces.
2. ⚠️ **[Reward hacking]** A behavior that isn't in [#10788](<https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10788>) or [David's decision gallery](<https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/dlwh/snowball-sft-decision-gallery/2026.10.23/index.html>): guessing what the hidden tests check, or recalling the upstream fix from memory. In 61.5% of the traces, we found this in 3 or more turns (10 or more in 8.6%). In some traces, the agent writes its final code to fit its guess about the tests rather than the issue.
3. 🔍 **[Cheating risk]** In some sandboxes, a newer release of the same project, which already contains the fix, is installed in `site-packages` or left in a `build/` folder. For example, the task repo is `mkdocs-include-markdown-plugin` `2.8.0`, while `3.4.1` sits in `site-packages`. The agent finds it and diffs it against the repo, so the trace shows a model looking at the answer. It's rare (roughly 0.1–0.3% of traces), and in the cases we read, the agent says it won't copy it.
4. 🚧 **[Newer revisions]** [Newer NVIDIA revisions](<https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Open-SWE-Traces/commits/main>) add `Qwen3.8-27B` traces on more harnesses (OpenHands, SWE-agent, Claude Code, OpenCode) and traces from `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`, which Marin doesn't use yet. I audited those too, and they'd need fixes first: in 8–18% of the `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` traces (depending on the revision), some turns carry reasoning text from a different conversation, and every OpenCode prompt ends with an extra `"`.

🙏 This is my first time contributing to Marin, so I'd appreciate a pointer on how best to hand this over. I've finished the audit and have per-trace results (which traces have which problems), but I'm not sure where they should go: upload them to HF as a dataset, open a PR that applies the fixes in the Open-SWE transform (maybe on top of [#10813](<https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10813>)), or something else?

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The Open-SWE adapter pins NVIDIA revision `f967cba` and keeps the two `Qwen3.8-27B` mini-swe-agent partitions. [PR #10813](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10813) already adds `resolved == 1` filtering; its transform does not repair prompts or apply the audit's quality flags. The [pinned NeMo-Skills template](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Skills/blob/592ebaec5a80e17a3535623d0f5704d29e13a64f/nemo_skills/prompt/config/eval/swe-bench/mini-swe-agent/swebench.yaml#L113-L127) contains “Solution Originality,” but the issue's prevalence estimates and the released-prompt mismatch still need trace-level verification.

**Relevant code**
- [Open-SWE source pin and partitions](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c10b671bc984abbc8eb154a37f9d83204fac8bf4/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/open_swe_traces.py#L21-L68) — input scope.
- [Open-SWE transform](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c10b671bc984abbc8eb154a37f9d83204fac8bf4/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/open_swe_traces.py#L79-L127) — filtering and `trajectory_id` provenance.

# Proposed Fix

1. Publish the per-trace audit as a versioned, revision-pinned ledger linked here. A Hugging Face dataset is suitable if it contains `trajectory_id`, partition, finding, affected turns, brief evidence, and scanner/review method; it need not duplicate the full traces. Include reviewed positives and negatives for each finding so the reported rates can be checked.
2. Validate prompt reconstruction on a stratified sample from both pinned partitions against the exact generation template and released system messages. If the missing section and insertion point are confirmed, send a focused follow-up PR after #10813 that restores only that prompt variant, bumps the transform version, and tests the rendered prompt and unaffected variants.
3. Review the reward-hacking and installed-fix flags separately before choosing keep/drop rules. Record reviewer decisions and retained documents/tokens by category; do not drop traces solely because a heuristic matches. Use the unchanged `resolved == 1` corpus as the control for a matched-budget training/evaluation comparison under [#10788](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10788).
4. Keep newer NVIDIA revisions outside this pinned-source fix. Gate each harness/model addition on checks for cross-conversation reasoning and malformed OpenCode prompts, then update the source revision in a separate PR.

The next handoff is the audit ledger and a few `trajectory_id` examples for each category. That makes the prompt PR and curation review reproducible without overlapping #10813.

spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
The SWE-smith Harbor task packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s` (and the same layout in `mlfoundations-dev/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests`) leave the repository's full git history in the agent's container. The image built from `environment/Dockerfile` keeps a local `main` branch with the unbroken code and about 944 other branches, so the agent can print the fix with `git diff HEAD main -- <package>` or `git show main:<file>`. `/tests` and `/solution` are correctly absent from the image.

Reproduce: build `swesmith-00003`'s `environment/Dockerfile` from the package, run it with no network, then `git log --oneline` (three commits: Initial commit, Bug Patch, Remove F2P Tests), `git branch -a` (944 branches including `main`), `git diff HEAD main -- oauthlib` (the exact fix).

Impact on existing data: in `open-athena/Kimi-2.5-swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s-maxeps-32k`, 860 of 5,237 passing trials (16.4%) and 433 of 4,119 failing trials run history-reading commands (`git show main:<path>`, diffs against `main` or `HEAD~N`, checkout or restore from history, `git log -p`). Some are benign (a diff against `HEAD~1` shows only the removed tests); many copy the original file. So the reported pass rate on these packages is inflated, and trace sets built on them carry shortcut solutions: the Kimi set above, the `GLM-4.7` and AgentTrove swesmith streams, and the allkimi relay data (`laion/calibforge-relay-traces`, `kimi_swesmith` rows) that was DARE-grafted into Snowball v0 (`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12`). SWE-bench Verified is not affected: there the fix is not in the repository's past.

A plain squash is not enough, because `tests/test.sh` itself uses history (`git checkout <task branch>; git checkout HEAD~1`) to restore the removed fail-to-pass tests before running pytest.

Expected: during the agent phase the repository has one commit, no other branches, no remote and no reflog; the verifier restores the fail-to-pass tests from outside the agent's view (for example, ship the test files in `tests/` and copy them in, or keep a git bundle that only the verifier unpacks). For each task, the gold patch still passes, the unpatched repository still fails, and the history-reading commands above return nothing.

Done when: a fixed package build exists with that validation on a sample of tasks, existing SWE-smith pass rates and training sets built on the leaky packages are re-reported with history-reading trials removed or flagged, and the shootout pool in #10213 uses the fixed packages.

# Research

The reported `swesmith-00003` image retains the pre-bug `main` branch and earlier commits, so an agent can recover the fix from Git history. Removing old refs alone is insufficient if the object database still contains the clean tree; the current verifier also uses `HEAD~1` to recover fail-to-pass tests. The reported 860/5,237 passing and 433/4,119 failing history-reading trials are contamination candidates, not yet an audited count of trials that copied the fix. Marin consumes these external packages and traces, while the package builder is outside this checkout.

**Relevant code and artifacts**
- [DCAgent package release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s) — affected task source.
- [Shootout #10213](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213) — waits for stripped packages.
- [AgentTrove ingestion](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/agenttrove.py#L17) — SWE-smith trace consumer.
- [Relay source PR #10027](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10027) — registers Kimi SWE-smith rows.

# Proposal

## Outcome

Publish an immutable, revision-pinned Harbor package release whose agent image contains the bugged working tree in one new Git repository with one commit, one task branch, no `main`/remote/tags/reflog, and no recoverable old objects. Keep the fail-to-pass test payload in Harbor's verifier-only `tests/` area and copy it into the repository when scoring. Record the old and new package revisions and per-task content digests; do not overwrite the release used by existing trials.

## Plan

1. Change the package producer to create a fresh `.git` after applying each bug patch, rather than squashing the existing repository in place. Export required test files from the source package into verifier-only storage before discarding history. Make `tests/test.sh` restore those files without `git checkout` or `HEAD~1`; keep `solution/` and `tests/` out of the agent container.
2. Validate a stratified sample across repositories and test layouts in offline Harbor runs. In each agent image, require one reachable commit and no old refs, remotes, reflogs, or dangling objects containing the clean fix. Exercise `git show main:<file>`, `git diff HEAD main -- <package>`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git log -p`, and `git fsck --unreachable`; none may reveal the clean file. For each sampled task, the untouched bugged tree must score 0 and the gold patch must score 1 under the revised verifier. Publish task IDs, package digests, commands, and results with the new release.
3. Audit the Kimi, GLM-4.7, AgentTrove, and allkimi relay/Snowball v0 provenance at trial or row level. Classify history commands as benign inspection, fix recovery, or unresolved; report raw and unflagged success rates with denominators, plus counts by outcome and category. Publish flagged row IDs or a reproducible manifest and clean-filtered trace revisions where the source can be republished. Annotate existing model and dataset results; filtering rows cannot undo training already performed on Snowball v0.
4. Pin the fixed package revision in the #10213 SWE-smith pool and block the eight-attempt generation until the package validation passes. Keep the already stated pilot-trace history filter separate from the new pool validation. Coordinate Harbor release acquisition with [#10198](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10198); its cache work does not repair the package contents.

## Risks and open questions

The package producer and release permissions are external to this repository, so the new dataset revision needs an owner with access to that build pipeline. The verifier payload must be checked against every sampled task's required test files; a one-commit image can still give false rewards if a file is omitted. Excluding all history-reading trials gives a conservative subset, not an unbiased replacement for a fresh evaluation on fixed packages.

- `environment/Dockerfile`: after the upstream `git fetch && git checkout <instance>`, the same `RUN` replaces the repository: `rm -rf .git && git init && git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main && git add -A && git commit -m "Initial commit" && git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc --prune=now`. This is a new `.git`, not a squash, so no old objects remain in the container's filesystem. The base image's lower layers still hold the old `.git`, but the container cannot read them.
- `tests/f2p_restore/`: the files that the upstream `git checkout HEAD~1` would change, at their parent contents, plus `deleted.txt`. They are computed from a bare clone of `github.com/swesmith/<repo>`. On `swesmith-00003` they match the image's own `git show HEAD~1:<path>` byte for byte.
- `tests/test.sh`: `git checkout <instance>; git checkout HEAD~1;` is replaced by `cp -a /tests/f2p_restore/files/. /testbed/` plus the deletions. The rest is unchanged. Harbor uploads `tests/` only to the verifier (checked in harbor 0.24.0 `verifier/verifier.py`; only `agents/oracle.py` uploads `solution/`).

**Validation** on 20 pool tasks, one from each of 20 repos, in local Docker following Harbor's phase order:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent-phase repository: 1 commit, 1 branch, 0 remotes, empty reflog, no `HEAD~1`/`main~1`/`origin/main`/`master` | 20/20 |
| Gold patch (`solution/solve.sh`) then `tests/test.sh`: reward 1 | 20/20 |
| Unpatched tree: reward 0 | 19/20 |
| Leak commands (`git log --all -p`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git diff HEAD main`, `git diff HEAD~1`, `git fsck --unreachable --lost-found`, `git stash list -p`, `git show main:<every file>`) print a clean-only line | 0/20 (upstream `swesmith-00003` control: 2/2) |

- "Clean-only line": a source line the Bug Patch removed that occurs nowhere in the bugged tree. 7 of the 20 tasks have none, so only the ref checks apply to them.
- The filesystem search found no git leak. It did find copies of clean lines in installed packages: `setuptools/_vendor/typeguard` is an older vendored typeguard, which is relevant for `agronholm/typeguard` tasks (57 in the pool). The `_pytest` (iniconfig) and `rapidfuzz` (thefuzz) hits are probably coincidental.

Per-task results: `pool/swesmith-validation-20.jsonl` and `pool/swesmith-leak-probe-20.jsonl`.

**TMax: same class of leak, different mechanism.** In `allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K@848e2182` `tasks.zip`, 221 of 2,200 environments build verifier assets into the agent's image (for example `/opt/oracle/<reference program>`, `/app/verifier/ground_truth_valid_events.txt`, `/home/user/oracle.py`), and `test_final_state.py` reads them. 🤖 The public `github.com/swesmith` mirrors are now unreachable while the agent runs, and a second leak was found in mini-swe-agent's own install.

**TL;DR**
- During the agent phase, the sandbox can reach only the model proxy. github.com, PyPI, apt and every other host fail DNS, and direct-IP HTTPS (GitHub 140.82.112.3, 140.82.114.4; 1.1.1.1) has its TLS handshake cut. Setup and the verifier keep full network.
